title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Grothendieck's 1981-82 programme of 'deploying' (déploiement) a stratified space. A conical singular space is to be replaced by an object built from manifolds with boundary or corners, glued by proper maps. Esquisse d'un programme §5 announces exactly such a 'dévissage' of stratified structures.

The previous page started an equivalent, intrinsic axiomatisation, and this page rewrites it. The datum is a separated (Hausdorff) topological space Σ with a strict order relation x<y. Let Σ*(1) ⊂ Σ×Σ be the graph of <, with source and target maps s(x<y)=x and b(x<y)=y. Σ*(2) is the space of chains x<y<z.

The axioms are:
(a) for every x, Σ_{<x} is a finite ordered set; the previous page says totally ordered.
(b) b: Σ*(1)→Σ is a proper 'bordant immersion', i.e. locally the inclusion of a boundary hypersurface. Hence b^{-1}(x) ≅ Σ_{<x} is compact and discrete, so finite.
(c) If z_α are the points of b^{-1}(x), the germs at x of the images b(Σ*(1), z_α) form a transversal family of bordant subspaces. Concretely, near x the space Σ looks like a corner of codimension k = |Σ_{<x}|, with one boundary hypersurface for each predecessor of x.
(d) Crossed out and rewritten. The map p (from the previous page's cartesian square Σ*(2)→Σ*(1)) is transversal to the proper bordant immersion b. A margin note asks for this 'in the strong sense', for all z_α over the same x.

Three special cases are then singled out:
1° Equisingular: s: Σ*(1)→Σ is proper and fibrant. Its fibre over x is Σ_{>x}, morally the (resolved) link of the stratum at x.
2° Non-singular: Σ is a manifold with boundary (really with corners), whose boundary is b(Σ*(1)).
3° Both together: s is a proper fibration whose fibres are manifolds with boundary. The fibrewise boundary is the image of the face map Σ*(2)→Σ*(1), (x<y<z)↦(x<z). Grothendieck adds that this is 'no doubt a consequence of the conjunction of 1° and 2°'.

In modern terms, Σ is the disjoint union of all resolved strata, each a manifold with corners. A pair x<y means that y lies on a boundary face of a higher resolved stratum lying over the point x of a lower one. Each boundary face fibres over the lower stratum with fibre the resolved link, and links of links are encoded by chains. The spaces Σ*(n) form the nerve of a topological poset, and the cartesian squares are Segal-type conditions on the face maps. The whole deployment is thus packaged as one topological poset with conditions on d0 and d1. This is essentially an iterated fibration structure, or manifold with fibered corners, in the sense of Melrose and Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza, encoded in Grothendieck's own nerve language.
errors: Axiom (a) on this page says only 'finite ordered'; the total ordering of Σ_{<x}, stated on the previous page, is not restated. It does not follow from (b) alone, so it must be assumed or derived from the transversality in (c).

The claim that case 3° follows from 1°+2° is not justified and is not obvious. Σ being a manifold with corners and s a proper fibration does not by itself make the fibres Σ_{>x} manifolds with boundary; some submersion or transversality hypothesis on s relative to the corner structure is needed. Grothendieck himself hedges ('sans doute').

Axiom (d) is left syntactically incomplete ('transversal pour l'immersion bordante b'). The object that is transversal (presumably p or p1: Σ*(1)→Σ from the previous page) is not restated after the crossing-out.
The 'bordant immersion' as stated is really a corner-type condition: Σ must be a manifold with corners, not merely with boundary. Calling case 2° a 'variété à bord' is therefore loose terminology.

ideas.what: Encoding a deployed (resolved) stratified space as a single Hausdorff space with a strict order whose graph Σ*(1) has a proper boundary-immersion target map b and a fibrant source map s
ideas.modern_name: manifold with fibered corners / iterated fibration structure, phrased as a topological poset (nerve of a topological category)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Melrose (fibred corners, 1990s); Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza 2012; earlier resolutions by Verona (1984) and Thom–Mather control data
ideas.where_published: Only announced in outline in Esquisse d'un programme §5 (dévissage of stratified structures); the poset/nerve axiomatics are not published

ideas.what: Finiteness and total ordering of predecessors Σ_{<x}, with transversality of the boundary hypersurfaces they define (corner of codimension |Σ_{<x}|)
ideas.modern_name: depth stratification / corners indexed by chains of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in resolution of Thom–Mather spaces (Verona; ALMP; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka 'unzipping')

ideas.what: Fibrewise boundary of s: Σ*(1)→Σ identified with the image of the face map Σ*(2)→Σ*(1), (x<y<z)↦(x<z); links of links encoded by 2-chains
ideas.modern_name: compatibility of boundary fibrations at codimension-2 corners (iterated links); Segal-type face-map conditions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Melrose / ALMP (iterated fibration compatibilities); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (links and unzips)

ideas.what: Separation of the conditions into 'equisingular' (s a proper fibration) and 'non-singular' (Σ a manifold with corners)
ideas.modern_name: local triviality along strata vs. smoothness of resolved strata

missed.claim: Grothendieck packages the entire resolution of a stratified space as the nerve Σ*(•) of a topological poset. Conditions are placed on the face maps: s is a proper fibration, b is a proper boundary immersion, and the squares are cartesian. This anticipates presenting stratified spaces or their exit-path data by simplicial spaces with conditions on d0 and d1. The literature on manifolds with fibered corners (Melrose, ALMP, Debord–Lescure–Rochon) and on exit paths (Treumann, Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka) does not phrase the resolution as a single topological poset with such axioms.
missed.quote: Si Σ*(1) est le graphe de la relation x<y, et s,b : Σ*(1) ⇉ Σ sont les applications source et but, l'application b est une immersion propre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a compact intrinsic definition of 'resolved stratified space' as a topological category satisfying Segal-type conditions. This could bridge the analytic fibred-corners literature and the ∞-categorical exit-path and 'unzip' approaches.

missed.claim: Whether case 3° (fibrewise manifolds with boundary, boundary given by Σ*(2)) follows from 1° and 2° is left as a conjecture ('sans doute').
missed.quote: c'est sans doute la conséquence de la conjonction des deux conditions 1°), 2°)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a precise lemma about when a proper fibration compatible with a corner structure has fibres that are manifolds with corners. It is relevant to existence results for iterated fibration structures.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is essentially the now-known resolution of Thom–Mather spaces into manifolds with fibered corners. Grothendieck's encoding as a single topological poset with nerve conditions, from 1981-82, is an elegant formulation not found in this form in the literature, but it is an outline rather than a theorem.
transcription_corrections: In (c), the sentence should read roughly: 'alors la famille des germes en x des sous-espaces de Σ images par b des (Σ*(1), z_α) est une famille transversale de sous-espaces bordants'. 'bordants' is crossed and rewritten beneath; 'transversales' is crossed and rewritten above.
'transversal par : l'immersion bordante' is more likely 'transversal pour l'immersion bordante b: Σ*(1)→Σ (propre)', continuing the rewritten (d). The '(propre)' sits at the right margin.
In 1°, 'propre' is written in the margin near 'fibrant' and appears to qualify 'fibrant', not s.
In 3°, 'propre' is written above 'fibrant'. 'donné' replaces a crossed-out word before 'par (x<y<z)→(x<z)'.
In the left margin the note reads approximately 'au sens fort d'une immersion pour les z_α ∈ Σ*(1) au-dessus d'un même x ∈ Σ* ...'; it is attached to (d).
